canonicalRemotePaths.withdrawalResolution: financial-operations Edge Function with service-role-only internal RPC

findings.summary: The remote wallet projection, including full bank-account fields, is copied into localStorage.
Account holder, document, branch, account number and Pix key are stored as plaintext columns and copied into withdrawal snapshots.
Hardened RPC and Edge Function paths coexist with legacy backend handlers that perform direct table writes.
The browser creates withdrawal external IDs and event keys from Date.now and Math.random, so a lost response followed by a retry can use a new idempotency identity.
Wallet reads can swallow remote failures and render local or empty projections, obscuring the distinction between unavailable authority and a real zero balance.
The local repository and an older shared-runtime migration encode a fixed five-percent platform fee even though PAY-B03 parameters remain unapproved.
The legacy approval path can complete a withdrawal before a provider transfer and ignores wallet-adjustment failure, so it must remain noncanonical and unreachable for real authority.
No provider transfer, settlement receipt or remote reconciliation authority exists for production withdrawals.

mandatoryInvariants: Authenticated UUID sessions never create local financial outcomes.
A zero or empty wallet must never be shown as authoritative when remote authority is unavailable.
Available balance is derived from canonical immutable financial entries, not browser aggregation.
Bank-account secrets are not persisted in browser storage or returned unmasked after intake.
Withdrawal retries reuse a stable client request identity across reloads and uncertain responses.
Withdrawal completion requires provider-confirmed transfer evidence and reconciliation.
Support and admin users do not receive unrestricted raw bank-account fields.
No unapproved PAY-B03 commission, payout or negative-balance parameter becomes runtime authority.
